title: docs(blog): four hand-drawn SVG figures for 'The Ontology Is the Software' — three interfaces and one user, four places to one definition, the ontology-runtime architecture, the three routes — readable in both themes
body:
立卡门类别 ③ — 维护者直派的任务 (maintainer-directed task).

## Maintainer ruling (verbatim, untranslated)

> 基于这个核心叙事，官网是否应该做一个专门的页面？

> 或者 blog 中是否应该适当增加配图

> 同意

Given in session https://claude.ai/code/session_011hRnra93sK5Q2gTYYTbdJR on 2026-10-12. The seat recommended figures in the existing essay over a new dedicated page (the essay is already the canonical statement that the README, the ontology concept page and the compare page point at; its weakness is being text only; a second page would split one narrative across three places), and the maintainer agreed. No dedicated page is part of this card.

## What lands

Four figures added to `content/blog/the-ontology-is-the-software.mdx`, each placed after the paragraph that states its idea, each with a one-line italic caption under it and an accessible title and description. The prose is not rewritten; only the figures and their captions are added. The frontmatter (title, description, author, date, tags) does not change.

| # | Section of the essay (heading on main) | Figure | What it shows |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | `## Why now` | Three interfaces, one user | A timeline of three eras: terminals and forms (people adapted to the software), web and mobile (the software adapted to people), a conversation box (the software disappears into language); beneath them one band spanning all three, "the user was a person: the API written for a programmer, the documentation for a reader, the audit log for an auditor"; then a fourth, highlighted column: the agent, the first new user in forty years |
| 2 | `## What an enterprise actually wants to say` | Four places to one definition | Four source boxes on the left (in veterans' heads; in policy documents; in spreadsheets; in a few hundred thousand lines of code) joined by a bus into one dark box on the right, "One definition", listing its five parts: what we have, how it relates, what can be done, who may do it, what happens when |
| 3 | `## Why code recedes` | The ontology runs | The architecture: a large model writes the ontology (and what is written wrong does not ship), people define and approve it, the ontology (the enterprise's definition of itself, five parts) is run directly by the runtime (every call permission-checked and audited), agents call the runtime, and database, API, UI and the tools agents call all derive from the ontology |
| 4 | `## What it is not` | Three routes for enterprise knowledge | Train it into the model (knowledge in the weights: change a rule, retrain; nothing to inspect; change the model, lose it all); keep it outside as a manual (knowledge graph or semantic layer: the model reads a description, acting needs another system, permissions yet another); keep it outside and it runs (ontology plus runtime: the model reads and writes it, the system runs it, agents act through it) |

The visual reference is the English deck's slides, which already draw these four pictures at 1920 x 1080 with inline styles; they are HTML in this container, readable by the developer, and are the source of the layout, labels and colour roles (not of the pixels: this card wants SVG drawn for the page, never screenshots):

- `/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-objectstack/1ddacfa2-cbe3-50df-b1b3-5e4cbf5ac646/scratchpad/deck-ontology-en/project/slides/scattered.html` (figure 2)

## Mechanism, with what was measured

- **Both themes.** The docs app switches theme with `next-themes` through fumadocs' `RootProvider` (`apps/docs/app/[lang]/layout.tsx`); `apps/docs/components/mermaid.tsx` reads `resolvedTheme` to re-render. The blog article body is `prose prose-neutral dark:prose-invert` (`apps/docs/app/[lang]/blog/[[...slug]]/page.tsx`). A figure must read correctly under that toggle, not under the OS preference: an SVG loaded through an `img` tag cannot follow the page's class, so the expected shape is inline SVG rendered by a React component registered in `apps/docs/mdx-components.tsx` beside `Mermaid`, with colours from `currentColor` and a small set of CSS custom properties or Tailwind `dark:` classes. Text in the figures at or above 4.5:1 contrast against its background in both themes, measured, not assumed.
- **The link lane.** `.github/workflows/check-links.yml` runs lychee `--offline` with `--root-dir` at `content/`, so a root-relative `/figures/x.svg` reference in the MDX would resolve to `content/figures/x.svg` and go red (the same reason the deck PDF link in this essay is absolute). Inline figures have no link to check; if a file reference is used anywhere, it is absolute.
- **Fonts.** Figures inherit the page's font stack (the prose column's), no font files, no web-font requests of their own.
- **Width.** Each figure sits in the prose column with a `viewBox` and 100 percent width, legible at phone width (the three-column figures may stack or scale; the author decides, and says which, with a measurement at 390 px).
- **Captions.** One italic line under each figure, the essay's register, no superlatives.
- **`check:docs-image-tag` is about Docker image tags, not pictures**; it will run because the file surface touches `content/`, and it is not affected by this card.

## Guardrails for the author

- File surface: `content/blog/the-ontology-is-the-software.mdx` (figure placements and captions only), new files under `apps/docs/components/` for the figures, and `apps/docs/mdx-components.tsx` for the registration. No `packages/**`, no `content/docs/**`, no `README.md`, no `apps/docs/public/**`, no CHANGELOG, no binaries.
- English only. No model identifiers anywhere.
- Every label in a figure is a phrase the essay or the deck already uses; no new claims, no numbers.
- Build the docs app and open the essay in both themes with the preinstalled Chromium (never `playwright install`): report the four figures' rendered sizes at 1280 px and 390 px, and the measured text contrast in both themes.
- Gates derived with `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` from the real change set, every one run; the docs build (`pnpm --filter @objectstack/docs build`) under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` must pass.
- Changeset: nothing publishes; `skip-changeset` once `packages/**` is confirmed untouched.
- Serial constraint: PR #22942 (the deck PDF refresh, in flight, `apps/docs/public/decks/` only) does not touch these files; no other open PR touches the essay or `apps/docs/components/`.

## Non-goals

- A dedicated narrative page on the site (decided against for now; revisit after the talk).
- The landscape figure (four cells) on the compare page; a later card if wanted.
- Changes to the deck, the README, the home page, or the Chinese site (objectos.ai is a separate project).

## Who acts

domain:devx lane, this seat, one os-dev dispatch at the derived tier, one draft PR. Precedent on the same page: #22263 via PR #22264 (the deck link at the end of the essay); precedent for a client-rendered figure component: `apps/docs/components/mermaid.tsx`.
